body.p: Amendments to the ClaimsThis listing of claims will replace all prior versions and listings of claims in the application:

br.br:
1. (Canceled)
2. (New) A method for cutting a transverse carpal ligament in a patient, the method comprising:
advancing a distal end of a shaft of a soft tissue cutting device into a carpal tunnel in the patient;
depressing a balloon activation lever on a handle of the soft tissue cutting device, to activate a bellows in the handle and thus inflate two balloons on either side of the shaft, the shaft extending from the handle;
deploying a blade out of the shaft, between the two balloons, to cut the transverse carpal ligament;
moving the blade back inside the shaft;
deflating the two balloons; and
removing the shaft of the soft tissue cutting device from the patient.
3. (New) The soft tissue cutting method of claim 2, further comprising:
before advancing the distal end of the shaft, priming the soft tissue cutting device by filling, via a fill port on the handle the two balloons with a gas or a fluid; and
allowing the balloon activation lever to move to an extended position to cause the gas or the fluid to move from the two balloons into the bellows.
4. (New) The soft tissue cutting method of claim 2, wherein deploying the blade and moving the blade comprises sliding a slider along the handle of the soft tissue cutting device, wherein the slider is coupled with the blade.
5. (New) The soft tissue cutting method of claim 2, further comprising verifying placement of the distal end of the shaft of the soft tissue cutting device with respect to one or more anatomical structures before inflating the two balloons.
6. (New) The soft tissue cutting method of claim 2, wherein the two balloons expand radially outwardly from the shaft and are located on a distal portion of the shaft, at or near a working end of the blade.
7. (New) The soft tissue cutting method of claim 2, wherein deploying the blade out of the shaft comprises moving a slider button coupled with a proximal end of the blade along the handle to cause the blade to slide along a blade guideway within the shaft and thus cause a blade working end to protrude out of a slot on the shaft.
8. (New) The soft tissue cutting method of claim 2, wherein depressing the balloon activation lever on the handle unlocks the blade to enable it to be deployed.
9. (New) The soft tissue cutting method of claim 2, further comprising locking the balloon activation lever in a locked position via a spring-biased button on the balloon activation lever, to lock the two balloons in an inflated state.
10. (New) The soft tissue cutting method of claim 9, further comprising releasing the spring-biased button before deflating the two balloons.
